summary: This article explains why millions of birds migrate over the Arabian Peninsula each year, how big and small birds make the trip, how they find their way, and where they rest.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “Birds That Fly Over Arabia: Migration” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: a long trip that animals make at the same time each year
a route in the sky that many birds use when they migrate
to fly high in the air, often without flapping

challengeTerms.def: a narrow stretch of sea that connects two larger bodies of water
to find and follow a route from one place to another
a column of warm air that rises from the ground

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that protecting wetlands and oases is important for birds that do not even live here? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Compare how big soaring birds and small birds like swallows make their long journey.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review migration, flyway, and soar, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses strait, navigate, and thermal to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
